analysis.title: US Equity Strategy 'Outlook 2027: After the derating, how to invest'
key_insights: The S&P 500 forward P/E fell about 20% in 2026 even as 2026 EPS is on track to grow about 33%. UBS attributes the derating to AI ROI and regulatory concerns, a spike in yields and credit spreads, higher oil and a drop in net buybacks.
The midterms added a new risk: state-level pauses put about 30% of US data center capacity additions in 2028 at risk.
In years after a fall of more than 10% in the SPX P/E, SPX has returned a median 20% with few negatives, and the P/E recouped about 30% of the decline.
UBS forecasts SPX EPS growth of 18% to $430 in 2027 and 14% to $490 in 2028. NVDA, MU and AVGO alone account for about 45% of next year's growth.
UBS keeps its end-2027 S&P 500 target at 8900, about 18x its 2028 EPS of $490. The end-2028 target is 9600, on 17.5x 2029 EPS of $550.
Data center pauses skew 2028 risks lower. Policy details are unlikely before next year, so UBS will revisit forecasts as they emerge.
AI capex concerns hit the AI trade even as demand accelerated. Annualized q/q cloud growth nearly tripled to about $86bn in Q3 from about $31bn in Q1.
UBS expects the Fed to hike twice, which should reduce rates volatility. It sees eventual Iran de-escalation as more likely than escalation.
Net buybacks fell about $120bn from Q1 to Q3. UBS expects a $200-400bn rebound next year on surging cash flow, with the big Semis adding $170bn+.
The main risks are slowing AI capex and a further yield spike. UBS says more downside looks priced after this much derating.
UBS estimates AI revenue potential at about $2.5tr in 5 years at the midpoint, above the $2tr low hurdle needed to justify $6-8tr of capex.
UBS prefers Semis over Tech Hardware because Semis' P/E has collapsed, pricing a fall in profits.
UBS is overweight Software, now mostly the AI application layer, with P/E to growth near 15-year lows. It also likes Hyperscalers, which own scarce compute amid rising capacity headwinds.
NDX over RTY is a higher-conviction view. NDX EPS has risen about 2x more than RTY's, and its P/E is back near 2022 lows.

UBS favors growth plus quality at a discount. Growth and CFROI spreads have widened while valuation spreads are average, and quality, momentum and growth tend to lead as expansions mature. Value and high beta are funding sources.
UBS is overweight Healthcare, which tops its REVS rankings as BioPharma sales growth rises. It funds the position with Staples, since Healthcare trades at about half Staples' P/E to sales growth.
UBS reduces Energy after a rally of about 40%, saying it screens rich versus fundamentals.
UBS names baskets to implement the views: AI Exposed Semis, AI Software Pioneers, Growth+CFROI at a Discount over Expensive Fundamentals, and Longevity & Wellness for Healthcare.
